FRT.thesis_one_line: Federal Realty's shopping centers keep raising rents and its 59-year dividend streak continues, but shares are fairly priced now, not a bargain.
kill_criteria: Comparable POI (same-property NOI) growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters (below the recent 2.8-4.9% band).
Net debt/EBITDAre above ~6.5x, or any covenant cushion closing to within 25% of its minimum/maximum.
A cut (not merely a tighten) to FFO/Core FFO guidance vs. the immediately preceding quarter.
Occupancy or leased rate down >100bp YoY for two consecutive quarters.
The 59-year dividend-increase streak broken, or payout >90% of Core FFO.
key_adverse_facts: Net debt is $4,660.7m at 2026-06-30, down 3.6% from $4,835.7m at 2025-12-31 (up 8.1% only year on year); net debt/EBITDAre sits at ~5.3x; cheap legacy debt (1.25% coupon, $400m repaid 2026-02-17) was refinanced into a materially higher-cost term loan/revolver draw -- a structural interest-expense headwind. [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4: earlier text said net debt rose 8.1% in two quarters]
Headline EPS is increasingly driven by gains on sale/asset recycling ($20.6-113.3m/quarter in Q1-Q2 2026) rather than organic FFO, raising execution/timing risk as portfolio turnover accelerates.

Corrected valuation removes the statistical-cheapness argument entirely: FRT now trades at ~14.9x P/FFO, near its own 37th(10y)/56th(5y) percentile and in line with the 15.1x REG/KIM/SPG peer median -- no margin of safety remains versus fundamentals alone.

The 2026-08-11 8-K is a $460m issue of 3.500% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2031 (exchange price ~$138.54, capped call to $165.07); reviewed by DVH4 2026-10-06. The full FY2025 10-K critical-audit-matters/related-party/Form 4 review was not completed in the dossier's time-boxed pass.
data_conflicts: V1's P/FFO(proxy) of 10.80x and 5.65th-percentile 'near cheapest ever' reading were artefacts of a proxy (GAAP NI + total D&A) that does not exclude realty gains-on-sale; V2R's NAREIT-FFO reconstruction corrects this to 14.94x TTM P/FFO and a 37.2/55.7 (10y/5y) percentile -- FRT is fair, not cheap.

V1's stated retail-REIT peer median of 31.29x (flagged as implausible in the dossier's own Section 7) is confirmed wrong by V2R: the real peer median (REG/KIM/SPG) is 15.07x, roughly half of V1's figure.

The b1 quant model's fam_V (value) factor score of 0.714 (Section 3) was corroborated by the same flawed V1 percentile and should likely be discounted alongside the P/FFO reading, though the factor re-score itself was not rerun this pass.
FRT.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the operating momentum (leasing spreads, occupancy, 8-for-8 guidance raises/maintains) is primary-source-verified and durable, but the corrected valuation removes the statistical margin-of-safety that supported the prior medium-high confidence; net debt has fallen for two quarters (-3.6% since year-end) but refinancing is at higher rates. [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's 'attractive' verdict and 5.65th-percentile 'near cheapest ever' claim were driven by a P/FFO proxy (GAAP NI + total D&A) that wrongly counted FRT's Q1-Q2 2026 realty gains-on-sale ($20.6-113.3m/quarter) as recurring FFO. V2R's NAREIT-FFO reconstruction corrects this to 14.94x TTM P/FFO (14.70x on FY26 Core FFO guidance), a 37th(10y)/56th(5y) percentile, in line with the 15.07x REG/KIM/SPG peer median. FRT is fair, not a statistical bargain; V1's verdict does not survive, and the dossier's verdict is downgraded from INCLUDE to INCLUDE-SMALL accordingly.

FRT.scenario_basis: DVH4 2026-10-06: V1 year-3 FFO/share (7.73 / 9.18 / 10.91) with exit P/FFO 12.5x / 14.9x / 17.0x (corrected own-history and peer median ~15x) and 3 years of dividends ($4.64 growing 0% / 3% / 5%) on a $110.52 price. V1 had 12.6x / 19.6x / 23.6x exit multiples (from a 31.9x NTM P/E peer proxy) and no dividends: -4.1% / +17.7% / +32.6%.

HST.thesis_one_line: Host owns top hotels with a beat-and-raise year and an improved credit rating, but 2026 is World Cup-flattered, the shares are fairly valued (about 3.4% a year of free-cash-flow growth priced in against a 2.5% base) and 2027 comparisons are harder.
kill_criteria: Comparable hotel RevPAR growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the core, most-watched KPI).
Adjusted FFO/share guidance is cut (not just raised more slowly) at any quarterly release -- a genuine reversal, not merely deceleration.
Net debt/EBITDAre rises above ~4.0x (current: 2.95x net debt/EBITDA on ratios.py) without an offsetting asset-sale plan.
The regular quarterly dividend ($0.20/share) is cut.
FY2027 comparable RevPAR growth guidance (first given around Feb 2027) comes in below roughly 2% -- the specific, falsifiable test of the '2026 was FIFA-flattered' bear case.
FY2027 Adjusted FFO per share guidance (about Feb 2027) comes in below the FY2026 guide mid-point of $2.165, i.e. AFFO per share is guided to decline (added 6 Oct 2026, RA12).
key_adverse_facts: Corrected valuation confirms HST is priced at the median of its own 10-year P/FFO range (48.8th percentile) and essentially at the peer median (10.95x vs 10.63x) -- not statistically cheap on any basis, removing the one input (V1's 29.2nd-percentile reading) that had supported the original 'attractive' framing.

FY2026's RevPAR/AFFO acceleration is partly a one-time FIFA World Cup effect; management's own words: 'year-over-year comparisons are expected to moderate' into H2 2026 -- FY2027 is a genuinely harder comp.
Sourced FY2025 ROE (11.2%) is ~500bps below the 16.1% TTM figure feeding the preliminary quant Quality score, inflated by the Q1 2026 $242m disposition gain.
Group booking volume described as 'soft' repeatedly across FY2025 releases; Maui properties still described as 'recovering' from 2023 wildfires as of the Q4 2025 release.

Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA12): the cash-flow basis in the dossier was wrong. FY2025 operating cash flow was $1,510m (the $1,607m quoted is trailing twelve months), FY2025 FCF $893m, FY2026E free cash flow to the firm about $1.09bn after $590m capex, $26m stock compensation and one-offs; at a 9.0% WACC the price implies about 3.4% a year of growth, at or above the 2.5% base, so there is no valuation margin of safety.
data_conflicts: V1's P/FFO(proxy) of 8.49x and 29.2nd-percentile 'attractive' reading were artefacts of the same proxy flaw: HST's Q1 2026 $242m gain on the 3-hotel sale inflated trailing GAAP net income and hence V1's FFO proxy. V2R's NAREIT-FFO reconstruction (built from 8 quarters of company-reported actuals) corrects this to 10.63x TTM P/FFO and a 48.8th(10y)/57.4th(5y) percentile -- squarely average, not cheap.

The dossier's own Section 7 peer comparison (10.4x FY26 AFFO guide, in line with PK/RHP/APLE) already anticipated the corrected reading almost exactly (10.36x) -- the correction resolves what the lead's prior reconciliation note (lead_holding_notes.json) treated as merely 'different reference points, not a contradiction' into a confirmed, non-contradictory match.
Pre-existing, unresolved conflict (dossier Section 3): preliminary quant Quality/ROE input (16.1%) vs sourced FY2025 GAAP ROE (11.2%) -- unaffected by this valuation correction, still flagged.

The dossier's '+1.7%/yr at WACC 7.5%' is V1's 1.75% (WACC 9.27%, trailing capex $249m from the D3 field) mislabelled; actual trailing capex is about $562m (FY26 guide $550-630m). Corrected at WACC 9.0%: 3.4% on FY2026E FCFF, 1.3% on TTM FCFF (RA12).
HST.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the beat-and-raise RevPAR/AFFO cycle, Baa2 upgrade and 2.95x net debt/EBITDA are unaffected, but the corrected cash-flow reverse DCF (about 3.4% implied vs 2.5% base, in_line) leaves no valuation margin of safety, and FY2026 is flattered by the World Cup; hence half weight

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's 'attractive' verdict and 29.2nd-percentile reading were driven by the same proxy flaw: HST's Q1 2026 $242m gain on its 3-hotel sale inflated trailing GAAP net income and hence V1's FFO proxy. V2R's reconstruction (built from 8 quarters of company-reported NAREIT FFO) corrects this to 10.63x TTM P/FFO (10.36x on FY26 AFFO guidance), a 48.8th(10y)/57.4th(5y) percentile -- squarely average, and matching this dossier's own already-published peer read (10.4x, 'in line ... not at a premium') almost exactly. V1's specific verdict does not survive, though it was never this dossier's primary support, so the INCLUDE verdict itself is unchanged. Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA12): reverse DCF redone on FCFF (AFFO less stock compensation, one-offs and $590m capex plus interest) at EV $19.34bn and WACC 9.0% (rf 5.17%): implied growth 3.4% on FY2026E ($1.09bn), 1.3% on TTM ($1.28bn); base 2.5%; implied_vs_base in_line.

HST.scenario_basis: Annualised 3-year total return from $22.42 on AFFO/share $2.165 (FY26 guide mid-point) with AFFO growth -5%/+2%/+6% a year, exit P/AFFO 8.5x/10.4x/11.5x and $0.80 a year of regular dividends (RA12, own arithmetic; replaces the un-annualised $20.50/$25.90/$32.20 values).
